title: Elucidating the molecular mechanisms underlying Sterigmatocystin-induced hepatocellular carcinoma through multi-omics integration and experimental validation
content:
Abstract
Sterigmatocystin (STE) is a food-borne mycotoxin with global prevalence, posing a potential risk of hepatocellular carcinogenesis. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying STE-induced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain elusive. In this study, four potential core targets—HSP90AB1, NSMCE2, PI4KB, and STARD3—were identified through an integrated strategy combining multi-omics analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and machine learning. All four targets are highly expressed in HCC tissues and exhibit favorable diagnostic value; notably, PI4KB and STARD3 expression correlates with patient prognosis and tumor stage, and displays heterogeneous expression across HCC cell subpopulations. In silico molecular docking and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations suggested a potential structural basis for the binding of STE to PI4KB and STARD3. In vitro experiments confirmed that STE induces reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, upregulates the DNA damage marker γ-H2AX, and increases the mRNA expression of PI4KB and STARD3 in hepatocytes. Collectively, this study preliminary elucidates the potential mechanism by which STE mediates hepatotoxicity and carcinogenic potential through regulating core targets, providing theoretical and experimental evidence for the prevention and control of STE-induced hepatotoxicity and HCC (Graphaic Abstract).
